verdict.rationale: The R2-first, separate R1 same-vessel retrieval, evidence/abstain/recapture/stop route is coherent as a long-term target; current project state does not support new implementation, experiments, or completion claims.

clauses: A6.16: final A-C relation is determined by direct-contact evidence and historical adjacency truth.
A6.15 memory table: R0/R1/R2/UNKNOWN posterior; R2 Local Memory stores pose/gap/contact and source_id.
A6.19/A6.20: old relations can be revised and R1/R2 swapped.
findings.finding: The plan conflates physical relation truth, epistemic UNKNOWN, model belief, and evaluator-only ground truth.
fix: Use R0/R1/R2 as adjudicated physical labels; UNKNOWN is missing label, insufficient evidence, or abstention, not a fourth physical relation.
In truth, same-object membership is transitive; R2 is a direct historical adjacency subrelation and is not transitive. Predicted R1/R2 edges stay soft.
For known pairs require P(R2)<=P(same-vessel) and class consistency: P(R2)=P(same)*P(adjacent|same), P(R1)=P(same)*P(known-nonadjacent|same). Unclosed adjacency cannot be turned into R1.

Online inference may use only permitted observation and predictions, never motherID, GT pose, true adjacency, or TruthPack. Store pose_hat and uncertainty; keep identity/provenance keys out of model features.
Beliefs may revise with a versioned evidence audit; historical truth changes only under GT correction/versioning or a new fragmentation event.

findings.finding: Style, material, thickness, profile, and repeated manufactured patterns can indicate a production class without identifying one physical vessel. Observationally exchangeable candidates are not deterministically identifiable.
fix: Add same-style hard negatives from distinct physical items, including same-mold/lot/production-context candidates.
Split by physical vessel and audit source/session/seed/background/ID shortcuts; do not expose mother identity online.
Add an identifiability/ambiguity subset and selective-risk reporting; permit UNKNOWN or a candidate ambiguity group when permitted observations cannot distinguish the true member.

clauses: section 2.2.2 requirement to account for missing physical pieces
findings.finding: Empty truth/prediction denominators are undefined, and physical-vessel closure is stronger than the stated database-snapshot task.
fix: Define V_G(q) as same-vessel members present in frozen gallery G excluding q; closure means all gallery entries have adjudicated membership. Track lost/unregistered physical pieces as provenance but do not require them to score catalog-snapshot retrieval.
Specify the four empty-set cases; score empty-gallery targets with false-member/false-acceptance risk and correct empty rejection, not fabricated P/R/F1 values.
Separate closed-snapshot main metrics from partial/open-world diagnostics and report eligibility/exclusion rates in the full workflow denominator.
Keep membership closure separate from R2 adjacency closure; use vessel/object/source clusters for macro averages and confidence intervals.

findings.finding: GT-neighbor context is privileged and may reveal object identity; it is a protocol-specific diagnostic, not a strict information-theoretic upper bound.
fix: Restrict Oracle-R2 to offline evaluator/diagnostic use; if teacher-forced training is run, label it separately and never call it deployable.
Match query, gallery, candidate pool, context count/degree/quality, observables, and compute.
Add degree/quality/source-matched shuffled-neighbor controls and, when feasible, same-count R1 context to separate direct-contact value from simply receiving a same-vessel member hint.
No production/test path may read motherID, GT poses, true adjacency, or TruthPack.

findings.finding: The percentage ladder does not define error denominators, class mix, source dependence, or the no-edge endpoint; its levels are not demonstrated realistic rates.
fix: Define separate FN among true R2 edges, FP per retrieved candidate/degree, R1↔R2 swaps, false membership edges, and correlated duplicate-source errors.
Retain 0/5/10/20/30% as stress levels, not realistic estimates; derive deployment corruption from frozen held-out predicted edges.
Add no-seed/empty-memory and all-edge-missing endpoints, with recovery to the static baseline, and report false-member injection plus coverage.

findings.finding: A single fixed-topology curve mixes observation corruption with physical interventions that can alter surfaces, current fit, fragment lineage, and contact topology.
fix: Separate fixed-world observation corruption (occlusion, blur, sensor noise, point dropout) from physical material loss/new chipping/secondary fracture.
For physical interventions preserve historical R2 facts by version/event, while recomputing current_fit_valid, evidence_visible, and new leaf/event relations.
Call uncalibrated 31-axis levels recipe/synthetic severity; map to physical severity only with independent measurement. Keep D5 real-domain confirmation separate.

clauses: A6.15 all-candidate token bank and multi-memory loop
findings.finding: The candidate space is broad relative to current readiness; equal FLOPs alone does not bound gallery search, repeated rereads, local-token residency, latency, or memory.
fix: B1 scalar feedback is a mandatory baseline, but a positive B1 gain is not required before B2 if a matched privileged-context diagnostic shows R1 information gain; scalar feedback may be an information bottleneck. In that case B2 is the only next minimal alternative and must be budget-matched to B1.

If the matched privileged-context diagnostic is null, audit candidate/context coverage, GT closure, metric power, and eligible-data capacity; if the protocol still shows no signal, stop this branch for lack of demonstrated signal/resource value without claiming universal absence of useful relation information.

Cache compact per-fragment embeddings, retrieve a common bounded Top-K shortlist, fetch local tokens on demand, and update only a bounded affected subgraph rather than materializing all N² relations/tokens.
Freeze K, local token budget, iterations, and per-query resource limits; report end-to-end FLOPs, P95 latency, peak VRAM/RAM, GPU hours, and query cost under the actual configured hardware.
Do not claim feasibility from RTX 5090 peak specs; official spec lists 32 GB VRAM and the document says throughput has not been measured.

findings.finding: The plan correctly rejects broad 'first autoregressive' claims. Existing 3D assembly work already describes iterative auto-agglomerative assembly, contact structure, geometric verification, and uncertain-part resampling; these works are related but not identical to R1 same-vessel retrieval.
fix: Keep novelty centered on a closed, identifiable R1 membership-retrieval task and safe, calibrated use of R2 context beyond a strong static/pairwise baseline.
Do not claim novelty from recurrence, feedback, graphs, or reversible edges alone.

findings.finding: Per owner-provided state, PG is 25–35% with the moving-front fieldrc/return_code mismatch and no retry; VF is 30–40% with native-CAD-source checking only; Objectivity source checking is PG-Frag scope; A12 is 30–40% with zero physically-qualified packs.
fix: Keep this route as a future hypothesis/contract. No implementation, new experiment, or new numeric claim in this closeout.

After closeout, eligible real observations plus closed membership GT are sufficient to consider real-data static/context experiments; a synthetic physically-qualified pack is required only for claims depending on physical synthetic generation, physical degradation, or synthetic pretraining.
Do not promote synthetic generation, vessel recovery, or physical degradation results to completed evidence until their relevant acceptance gates have passed.
